Definition: , or prolonged παριστάνω from G3844 and G2476; to stand beside, i.e. (transitively) to exhibit, proffer, (specially), recommend, (figuratively) substantiate; or (intransitively) to be at hand (or ready), aid:--assist, bring before, command, commend, give presently, present, prove, provide, shew, stand (before, by, here, up, with), yield.
BiblicalUsage: Paristemi means to stand beside, to present, to yield, to prove. Jesus stands beside His disciples after the resurrection and shows Himself alive in Acts 1:3. Paul tells the Romans in Romans 6:13 not to yield their members as instruments of unrighteousness, and in Romans 12:1 to present their bodies a living sacrifice. Timothy is charged in 2 Timothy 2:15 to show himself approved unto God, a workman who need not be ashamed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe standing beside is the posture of the whole Christian life: Christ stands beside us, and we stand beside Him, presenting what we are and yielding what we have. My position is that a body presented to God is not wasted, it is the only reasonable service.
